# agent-linters

> Rewrites linter output as short, imperative prompts, so a coding agent gets
> an instruction ("remove unused import `os`") instead of a screenful of
> diagnostics. Works at the tool layer — env vars, user-level config, two
> PATH shims — so it applies to any agent that shells out to a linter
> (Claude Code, Codex, or anything else) without configuring each one
> separately. POSIX `sh` + stdlib-only Python 3. No build, no test suite, no
> runtime dependencies. MIT licensed.

## Entry point

- `bin/lintp` — the CLI. Routes files by extension, runs the applicable
  linters, and prints one line per finding: `path:line  imperative sentence`.

  Routing table:
  | Extensions | Linter(s) |
  |---|---|
  | `.py .pyi` | ruff + mypy |
  | `.js .mjs .cjs .jsx .ts .tsx .mts .cts` | oxlint |
  | `.css .scss .json .jsonc` | biome |

  biome also lints JS/TS internally, but those findings are dropped — oxlint
  owns that ground, so a file never gets two conflicting prompts for the same
  problem.

  Flags: `--fix` (apply safe autofixes first, then report what remains),
  `--codes` (append the rule code to each line), `--strict` (add oxlint's
  `pedantic` and `style` categories), `--tools ruff,mypy,oxlint,biome` (run a
  subset).

  Exit codes: `0` clean (nothing found), `1` findings printed, `2` a linter
  itself failed to run.

  A project's own config always wins. ruff, mypy and biome each search
  upward for their own config file and `lintp` never touches that search.
  oxlint is the exception — it only checks the cwd — so `lintp` locates the
  nearest `.oxlintrc.json` (or `oxlint.json`/`.oxlintrc`) itself and passes it
  with `-c`, rather than forcing its own category flags on top of it.

## Rule phrasing tables

The imperative wording lives in four dicts near the top of `bin/lintp`, each
keyed by the linter's own rule code and mapping to a `(regex, template)` pair
(or an ordered list of them) that extracts values out of the linter's message
and renders the instruction:

- `RUFF_RULES` — Python, e.g. `F401` → "remove unused import `{name}`".
- `MYPY_RULES` — Python types, e.g. `return-value` → "return {want}, not {got}".
- `OXLINT_RULES` — JS/TS, eslint-style rule names, e.g. `jsx-key` → "add a
  `key` prop to the list element".
- `BIOME_RULES` — CSS/JSON. Rules absent from this table still get a
  camelCase-derived phrase (`noDescendingSpecificity` → "avoid descending
  specificity") rather than biome's longer explanatory sentence.

Any rule code absent from all four tables falls through to the linter's own
message text unchanged — nothing is ever swallowed; a missing entry degrades
gracefully instead of breaking.

## Shims

- `shims/mypy` — POSIX `sh` wrapper. Injects `--no-error-summary` (no env var
  exists for it) and gives each working directory its own `MYPY_CACHE_DIR`
  under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `~/.cache/mypy/<hash-of-cwd>`), so two
  projects with same-named modules (`utils.py`, `main.py`) never collide in
  one cache. `exec`s the real `mypy` found by walking `PATH` past itself, so
  exit codes pass through untouched.
- `shims/biome` — POSIX `sh` wrapper. Injects `--reporter=concise` for the
  `lint`, `check` and `ci` subcommands only (no env var or config key exists
  for biome's reporter); a caller-supplied `--reporter` makes it step aside.

## Install

`install.sh` symlinks `bin/`, `shims/` and `config/` into `~/.local` and
`~/.config`, and adds one `source` line to `~/.profile` and
`~/.config/fish/config.fish`. `--claude` additionally patches
`~/.claude/settings.json`'s `env` block via `jq`. `--uninstall` reverses all
of it, restoring any backed-up file. Re-running is idempotent.

## Requirements

POSIX `sh`, Python 3.8+, and whichever of ruff, mypy, oxlint, biome you use —
none are bundled. Linux and macOS.

## Full documentation

- [README.md](README.md) — install steps, the full trap list, and worked
  examples of generic linter advice that was wrong for a real codebase.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — how to add a rule phrasing, style
  requirements, PR checklist.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — actual threat surface (writes into `$HOME`,
  shims ahead of real binaries on `PATH`, `--claude`'s settings patch) and how
  to report an issue.
